body.html: Jint Place Hostel — the Thai name is Jin Place Hostel — is a budget hostel on Chayangkun Road (Highway 212, the Yasothon–Amnat Charoen route) at 576 Village No. 4 · It's a small, owner-run place that doesn't lean on design or upscale facilities, but sells the thing it does well: clean A/C rooms, covered parking right by your door, and friendly service for a few hundred baht · It suits people driving the Isan routes, travellers there for work, and anyone after a daily or monthly room on a budget.

Rooms are air-conditioned with a private bathroom, simply but cutely decorated and clean, with free Wi-Fi that several reviews call strong and smooth to use · What guests praise often is that the rooms are cleaner than the price suggests, the bathroom is roomy, and there's free laundry for guests — something you rarely get at this budget · There's a seating area to relax in, the vibe is easygoing, and some reviews mention a small welcome touch the owner lays on · Overall it feels warmer than a typical hotel in the same price band.

"Clean room, fast internet, covered parking against sun and rain right outside the door, and a kind owner who looks after you like a relative — great value at just over four hundred baht for a one-night stop."

Location is another thing self-drivers talk about · It's right on Chayangkun Road, the main route linking Yasothon and Amnat Charoen, easy to find and easy to get in and out of, near a PTT station and a 7-Eleven a few steps away for food and daily items · The parking is covered against sun and rain right by the room, spacious and well-lit, and several self-drivers say they feel at ease leaving the car there · It works both for travellers stopping over en route and for anyone wanting a monthly room near the main road.

To be straight with you, per real guest reviews: this is a small, owner-run hostel, so there are limitations worth knowing before you book · There aren't many rooms, the amenities are simple, and there's no 24-hour front desk, so if you're arriving late or checking in off-hours, call the owner ahead · It's on the main road outside the town centre, so getting to in-town sights such as the Ban Singha Tha old town or Phaya Thaen Park means a drive, not a walk · And as a newer place with few public reviews, there's limited information online, so confirm the details and price with the owner before booking.

In short: if you're after a budget hostel on the Yasothon–Amnat Charoen route with clean A/C rooms, parking right by your door, and a friendly owner-run feel — Jint Place Hostel is a fitting choice for a few hundred baht · The overall picture from real reviews lines up: "clean room, fast internet, good parking, kind owner, good value." · It suits drive-through travellers, people there for work, and anyone wanting a simple daily–monthly room more than someone planning a longer restful stay in a fully-equipped hotel.

A tip from following the reviews here: call the owner directly to check availability and price before booking, since it's a small place with both daily and monthly rates that vary by season and room · If you're driving, ask about the covered parking by the door so you're set · And if you plan to explore central Yasothon, allow time to drive in, as the hostel is on the main road outside the town centre.

faq.q: Where is Jint Place Hostel, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Jint Place Hostel (Jin Place Hostel) is at 576 Village No. 4, Chayangkun Road, the main route (Highway 212) linking Yasothon and Amnat Charoen · It's easy to find and easy to get in and out of, near a PTT station and a 7-Eleven a few steps away · In-town Yasothon sights such as the Ban Singha Tha old town and Phaya Thaen Park need a drive into town.

faq.q: How much does Jint Place Hostel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿400/night for a Standard A/C Room · A room with covered parking by the door runs about ฿500 · There are also monthly rooms for people there for work, with the monthly rate on request from the owner · It's a small place and prices vary by season and room type, so compare and ask before booking.

faq.q: Who is Jint Place Hostel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers driving the Yasothon–Amnat Charoen route, people there for work, and anyone after a budget daily–monthly room who wants a clean A/C room and easy parking · It's less suited to anyone wanting a big hotel with a pool, breakfast or a 24-hour front desk.

faq.q: Are the rooms clean and is the parking good at Jint Place Hostel?
faq.a: Most reviews say the rooms are clean and cutely decorated, the bathroom is roomy, and the Wi-Fi is strong · The parking is a frequent praise point: it's covered against sun and rain right by the room, spacious and well-lit, so self-drivers feel at ease leaving the car there.

faq.q: Does Jint Place Hostel have a 24-hour front desk, and how do you check in?
faq.a: There's no 24-hour front desk, as it's a small owner-run hostel · If you're arriving late or checking in off-hours, call the owner ahead to arrange the key and check-in · The owner looks after guests in a friendly, family-style way.

faq.q: What standout services does Jint Place Hostel offer?
faq.a: The highlights reviews mention are strong free Wi-Fi, free laundry, covered parking by the door, and a seating area · It's near a PTT station and 7-Eleven for food and daily items · The service is simple hostel-style but feels warmer than a typical hotel in the same price band.
